back: A separate sorted (or hashed) structure of some columns with pointers to rows, kept in sync on writes.
Reading every row of a table to answer a query.
Wide, shallow, balanced tree of pages; leaves sorted and linked for range scans.
Each page holds hundreds of keys, so 100M keys need about 3 levels.
Memtable + log, flush to immutable SSTables, merge by compaction.
A compact structure that says a key is definitely not in a set, letting reads skip files.
A composite index serves filters on its first column(s), in order.
Equality columns first, then the range or sort column.
Includes every column a query needs, so the table isn't touched (Index Only Scan).
Bytes written to storage ÷ bytes the app wrote; each index adds to it.
Most rows match the filter, so an index doesn't help.
Indexes only rows matching a condition, e.g. WHERE status = 'failed'.
Indexes a computed value, like lower(email), so queries using it can use the index.
EXPLAIN shows the planned route; ANALYZE runs it and shows real times and rows.
